title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Π̂ = Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, free profinite on two of the loops ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞, with ℓ_0ℓ_1ℓ_∞ = 1. ρ is the order-3 automorphism permuting the loops cyclically (ρ(ℓ_i) = ℓ_{i+1}, with 0→1→∞→0).

The groups:
- M^~_{0,3} is a group of automorphisms u of Π̂ that 'commute with ρ up to an inner automorphism'. That is, uρu^{-1} = int(g)∘ρ with g = g_u ∈ Π̂. The page writes this loosely as g = [u,ρ].
- M^{!~}_{0,3} is the subgroup of those u that send each ℓ_i to a conjugate of ℓ_i^λ, where λ = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ^* is the cyclotomic character.
- SM^{!~} consists of the quadruples (u, f_0, f_1, f_∞) with u(ℓ_i) = int(f_i^{-1})(ℓ_i^λ). Each f_i is determined up to the centralizer L_i ≅ Ẑ of ℓ_i, which gives the extension 1→Ẑ^3→SM^{!~}→M^{!~}→1 of the previous page.

The new subgroup: Grothendieck imposes the cocycle-type compatibility (11), f_{i+1}^{-1} = g ρ(f_i^{-1}), between the three conjugators.
- Since ρ^3 = id and Π̂ has trivial centre, (uρu^{-1})^3 = 1 forces gρ(g)ρ^2(g) = 1.
- Hence if (11) holds for two indices it holds for the third. This is the remark on the page, computed at the end of the previous page.
- The quadruples satisfying (11) form a subgroup S_0M^{!~}_{0,3}.
- Because f_1 and f_∞ are then determined by f_0, this subgroup is identified with the pairs (u, f_0) satisfying u(ℓ_0) = int(f_0^{-1})(ℓ_0^λ).

The remaining ambiguity is f_0 ↦ ℓ_0^n f_0. Via (11), and since ρ(ℓ_0) = ℓ_1, it propagates to the same shift n on each of f_1 and f_∞. This gives:
- an extension 1→Ẑ→S_0M^{!~}→M^{!~}→1;
- a morphism of extensions to the Ẑ^3-extension, which is the diagonal Ẑ→Ẑ^3, n ↦ (n,n,n).

So the Ẑ^3-extension is the pushout, along the diagonal, of the 'finer' Ẑ-extension.

Purpose: this sets up a ρ-equivariant parametrization of the 'braid-like' automorphisms by pairs (λ, f). The next page connects it to explicit systems (α, β, f) satisfying a relation of hexagon type (17), and to the normalizer of L_0. This is essentially a pre-Drinfeld construction of a lift of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (pairs (λ, f) with a 3-cycle relation), keeping the Ẑ-indeterminacy of f as an extension rather than normalizing f into the derived subgroup.
errors: Previous page (8) writes S_0M^~_{0,3} ⊂ M^~_{0,3}; the context shows it should be S_0M^{!~} ⊂ SM^{!~} (this page corrects this).

'[u,ρ] = g' is abusive notation: the actual relation is uρu^{-1}ρ^{-1} = int(g) in Aut(Π̂). The deduction gρ(g)ρ^2(g) = 1 needs the trivial centre of the free profinite group, which is used but not stated.

The subgroup property of S_0 (stability of (11) under composition) is asserted without verification. It is plausible because g_{uu'} = u(g_{u'})·g_u behaves as a cocycle, but this is not checked on the page.

Not remarked: the Ẑ-extension (13) can be trivialized by normalizing f_0 (e.g. requiring its ℓ_0-exponent in the abelianization to vanish), as in the standard GT normalization f ∈ F̂_2'. Whether this normalization is a group-theoretic splitting is not discussed.

ideas.what: Cocycle condition gρ(g)ρ^2(g) = 1 for the defect of commutation with the order-3 symmetry ρ, and the resulting rigidification of the conjugators f_i so that two of the three conditions imply the third
ideas.modern_name: 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m f(x,y)x^m = 1 in the definition of GT-hat
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches the idea of a 'Teichmüller tower' and its 0- and 1-dimensional generators/relations; no explicit relation of this form there

ideas.what: Group S_0M^{!~} of pairs (u, f_0) with u(ℓ_0) = f_0^{-1}... conjugate of ℓ_0^λ, viewed as a Ẑ-extension of M^{!~}, from which the Ẑ^3-extension of all conjugator choices is obtained by pushout along the diagonal
ideas.modern_name: Lifting outer GT-type automorphisms to automorphisms with chosen inertia conjugators; the indeterminacy of f modulo the inertia subgroup
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps treatments of GT-hat (normalizing f in the derived subgroup)

missed.claim: Explicit pre-Drinfeld (c. 1981, 'Longue Marche' sequel) construction of a ρ-equivariant group of pairs (λ, f) with a cocycle/3-cycle relation. The Ẑ-indeterminacy of f is kept as a central-type extension (diagonal in Ẑ^3) rather than killed by normalization. This documents that Grothendieck had an essentially GT-like parametrization with the 3-cycle relation.
missed.quote: il suffit qu'il le soit vérifié pour deux indices, pour que ce soit vérifié pour tous les trois
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence for Grothendieck's precursor of GT-hat. The 'unnormalized' Ẑ-extension viewpoint may relate to framed or ribbon variants of GT, but on this page it is mostly bookkeeping.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine rigidification step. Its interest is historical: a GT-like (λ, f) parametrization with the 3-cycle cocycle relation, written down well before Drinfeld. The existence of such material in Grothendieck's notes is broadly suspected but not documented in print.
transcription_corrections: Line 7: '(u ∈ M, f_0 ∈ Π̂_{0,3})' — M is presumably shorthand for M^{!~}_{0,3}.
(12): read λ = χ(u) (cyclotomic character), as transcribed.
In (15) the underlined n denotes elements of Ẑ: n_0 = n_1 = n_∞ = n.
